passages.title: From CJI To Cabinet Minister: How India's Election Commissioner Selection Process Changed
passages.passage:
From CJI To Cabinet Minister: How India's Election Commissioner Selection Process Changed
The process of appointing India’s Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) has undergone a significant change in the past few years, with the Chief Justice of India (CJI) moving from the selection panel to a Union Cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
That committee was to comprise the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and the Chief Justice of India. If there was no recognised Leader of the Opposition, the leader of the largest opposition party in the Lok Sabha was to be part of the panel instead.
The law retained a three-member selection committee but made one crucial change, that the Chief Justice of India was replaced by a Union Cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
The Supreme Court's March 2023 judgment held that appointments should be made on the advice of a three-member committee including the Chief Justice of India until Parliament enacted a law. Parliament subsequently passed the 2023 Act, which replaced the CJI with a Union Cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister.

passages.title: In 1911 , why did British India shift its capital from Calcutta to Delhi . Decoding the reasons behind the move
passages.passage:
In 1911, why did British India shift its capital from Calcutta to Delhi. Decoding the reasons behind the move
Today, Delhi is synonymous with political power in India. Parliament, the President's residence and the Union government's headquarters are all located in the city. However, more than a century ago, the seat of British power was elsewhere.
Until 1911, Calcutta was the capital of British India. That changed on December 12, when King George V announced at the Delhi Durbar that the seat of government would be transferred to Delhi. The decision also marked the beginning of the construction of an entirely new imperial city, which would come to be known as New Delhi.
At the beginning of the 20th century, Delhi was an important railway and commercial junction. Its railway network connected the city to several parts of the country. Travel to Shimla, the summer capital of British India, was also relatively convenient, with the hill station accessible by train.

New Delhi is the capital of India, and many will confuse Delhi with the capital of India, but their perception is wrong. Delhi is one of the union territories of India, which comprises a legislature, and officially it is called the National Capital Territory of Delhi (NCT), not the capital of India.

The government has questioned how such a massive liability has accumulated when the companies have consistently reported profits and have also paid dividends to the Delhi government, which holds equity in the distribution firms.

passages.title: Agra resort near Taj Mahal gets bomb threat, security vigil on
passages.passage:
Agra resort near Taj Mahal gets bomb threat, security vigil on
A resort hotel near Shilpgram, about a kilometre east of the Taj Mahal in Agra, received a threat via email on Thursday evening claiming that a bomb blast would take place there within seven days, police said on Friday.
Police, along with the bomb detection and disposal squad, fire department and dog squad, conducted an extensive search of the resort till late Thursday night but found nothing suspicious. However, security vigil will continue in view of the seven-day threat, an official said.
Yatendra Singh Nagar, assistant commissioner of police (ACP), Taj security, said the hotel received the email from an unidentified sender, threatening that a bomb had been placed in a room.
The email and details of the sender have been forwarded to the Agra police cyber cell for further investigation, Nagar said.
Based on a complaint lodged by the resort owner, a case was registered on Friday against unidentified accused at Tajganj police station under Section 351(4) BNS (criminal intimidation committed through anonymous communications or when the offender conceals their name or identity), officials said.

IN-SPACe Chairman Pawan Goenka on Sunday dismissed suggestions that the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) could see its significance reduced, saying the space agency would continue to serve as the foundation of India’s space programme.
ISRO said that claims suggesting an attempt to privatise the space agency or reduce its role are entirely baseless and incorrect.

passages.title: 'Isro’s role won’t diminish': Agency allays concerns over privatisation
passages.passage:
'Isro’s role won’t diminish': Agency allays concerns over privatisation
Two days after nine associations representing thousands of Indian Space Research Organisation (Isro) employees sought clarity on the privatisation of the space sector, IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka and Isro on Sunday said the space agency’s role would not diminish.
Goenka said there had been “some misleading narrative” in the media about Isro’s future role. “Let me say it unequivocally: ISRO’s role is by no means diminishing. It will remain the bedrock of Indian space sector. The reforms since 2020 are about expanding India’s overall space ecosystem,” he said in a post on X.
The employees’ associations had written to the Department of Space secretary and Isro chairman V Narayanan seeking clarity after Goenka said that “eventually, ISRO will not make any launch vehicles and will not manufacture any launch vehicles. That will all be done by the private sector or PSU.”
The agency said private-sector participation would enable the agency to focus on the next generation of India’s space programme while industry scales mature technologies.

Chandrayaan-3 May Have Landed On Moon's Oldest Craters, Says Researchers
India's lunar mission Chandrayaan-3 possibly landed in one of the oldest craters of the Moon, according to scientists who analysed images from the mission and satellites.
S Vijayan, an associate professor in the Planetary Sciences Division, Physical Research Laboratory, told PTI, "Chandrayaan-3 landing site is a unique geological setting where no other missions have gone. The images from the mission's Pragyan rover are the first on-site ones of the Moon at this latitude. They reveal how the Moon evolved over time".
In this case, Chandrayaan-3 was found to have landed within a crater -- about 160 km in diameter -- and detected in the images as a nearly semi-circular structure.
The Pragyan rover was deployed on the lunar surface by the Vikram lander, on board the Chandrayaan-3.
"Together, the images from the mission and satellites showed that the Chandrayaan-3 landing site consists of material deposited from different regions of the Moon," he said.

passages.title: Chandrayaan-3 rover lands in oldest crater where ‘no other missions have gone’; S.Vijayan says ‘shows how moon evolved'
passages.passage:
Chandrayaan-3 rover lands in oldest crater where ‘no other missions have gone’; S.Vijayan says ‘shows how moon evolved'
Chandrayaan 3: India's lunar mission has landed in one of the oldest craters on the Moon, scientists said on Saturday. The crater where ‘no other missions’ have gone, is 3.85 billion years old, said scientists.
“Chandrayaan-3 landing site is a unique geological setting where no other missions have gone. The images from the mission's Pragyan rover are the first on-site ones of the Moon at this latitude. They reveal how the Moon evolved,” said Vijayan, reported PTI.
An impact basin is defined as a large, complex crater with a diameter exceeding 300 km, whereas a regular crater is less than 300 km in diameter. In this instance, Chandrayaan-3 was found to have landed within a crater approximately 160 km wide, appearing in images as a nearly semi-circular structure.
On August 23, 2023, Chandrayaan-3 made a soft landing on the Moon's south pole. The GOI named the landing site as ‘Shiv Shakti Point’.

passages.title: Not Landing, ISRO Chief Says This Was 'Most Difficult' Part Of Moon Mission

Not Landing, ISRO Chief Says This Was 'Most Difficult' Part Of Moon Mission
Chandrayaan-3 successfully soft-landed on the Moon's surface at 6.04 pm Wednesday evening - a feat matched only by Russia (then the Soviet Republic), the United States and China - guaranteeing India pride of place in the global space race. Chandrayaan-3's nearly 400,000 km journey to the Moon culminated in a nerve-wracking final 20 minutes - the 'power descent' phase, which is an automated landing sequence carried out by the lander.
'Capturing the Moon' refers to the critical moments when Chandrayaan-3 must identify a landing site - in which it is aided by a slew of high-powered cameras developed inhouse by ISRO - while it deboosts from lunar orbit and prepares for descent.
A smiling ISRO chief then said, "The last critical moment, of course, you watched along with us", referring to the tense moments leading up to Chandrayaan-3's Moon soft landing.

passages.passage:

New study on Chandrayaan-3’s landing site reveals potential presence of primitive lunar mantle materials
The portion of Chandrayaan-3’s landing site taken by Vikram Lander after the successful landing. Photo: ISRO
In a new finding, scientists of the Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) have revealed that the landing site (Shiv Shakti point) of the Chandrayaan-3 mission is a promising site to access primitive mantle samples, which was otherwise lacking in the existing lunar collections.
PRL scientists made a detailed analysis of the abundances of these volatile elements and found the concentrations of sodium and potassium at the Chandrayaan-3 landing site was found to be much lower compared that found in the soil samples from lunar highlands in earlier missions (Apollo 16 and Luna 20), while the concentration of sulfur was found to be 300-500 ppm higher than in soils from Apollo 16 and Luna 20 missions.
“The anomalous differences in the concentrations of these volatile elements make it important to investigate the probable source that led to their enrichment or depletion at the Chandrayaan-3 landing site,” ISRO said.

passages.title: NASA shares new images of ISRO's Chandrayaan-3, first detailed look at the landing site on the Moon
passages.passage:
NASA shares new images of ISRO's Chandrayaan-3, first detailed look at the landing site on the Moon
On 27 August 2023, NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO) aimed its camera at a specific point on the lunar landscape. Its mission was to capture the Indian Space Research Organization's (ISRO) Chandrayaan-3 lander, which had touched down on the Moon just four days before that.
The orbiter succeeded, giving the world its first detailed look at the landing site, located a considerable distance of approximately 600 kilometres away from the Moon's South Pole.
In the images, a bright halo surrounds the Chandrayaan-3, making it particularly striking against the lunar surface. This halo is not just a photogenic quirk but is the result of the rocket plume interacting with the Moon's fine-grained soil, also known as regolith.
The Chandrayaan-3 mission has been a significant undertaking for ISRO, representing India's third lunar probe. Its landing on August 23 was a momentous occasion. The new images provided by NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter enrich our understanding of the mission's current status on the Moon.

As President-elect Donald Trump prepares to take the oath of office on Monday, Washington DC will be bracing for what reports say is likely to be one of the coldest inaugurations in recent history.
The forecast of extreme cold threatens to make Donald Trump's inauguration the coldest since Ronald Reagan’s second swearing-in ceremony in 1985. That year, temperatures were so extreme—reaching just 7 degrees by noon—that the ceremony was held indoors, and the planned parade was canceled. Reagan even joked about the weather in his inaugural speech, noting, "We would have been standing at the steps if it hadn’t gotten so cold."
Other cold inaugurations include John F Kennedy’s 1961 ceremony, which saw temperatures of 22 degrees with snow on the ground. In contrast, Trump’s first inauguration in 2017 was relatively milder, at 48 degrees, while Joe Biden’s 2021 inauguration registered 42 degrees.
Donald Trump, whose Republican Party swept the presidential election, will be inaugurated as US President on Monday, January 20.

passages.title: What Is the Ganga River Called in Bangladesh?

What Is the Ganga River Called in Bangladesh?
The Ganga is one of the most important rivers of India and Bangladesh. It originates in the Himalayas and flows through northern India before entering Bangladesh. After entering Bangladesh, the river is known by a different name. So, what is the Ganga River called in Bangladesh? Keep reading to read in detail.
The Ganga enters Bangladesh from the Indian state of West Bengal. After crossing the international border the river is generally known as the Padma. The river then flows through central Bangladesh before joining other major rivers.
The Padma and Meghna rivers meet in Bangladesh after the Padma has joined the Jamuna. The combined river system eventually flows towards the Bay of Bengal. This region forms part of the vast Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna river system and delta.

passages.passage:

Earthquake 2,500 years ago abruptly changed Ganga river’s course
In the Y-shaped feature at the centre of this image, the Ganga river is visible as the branch on the left, flowing towards the Sundarban Delta at the bottom. | Photo Credit: Google Earth
In 2018, geochronologist Elizabeth Chamberlain, an assistant professor at the Wageningen University & Research, Netherlands, and her team were in Bangladesh to study the movement of river channels in the Ganga delta. They were exploring an almost 2-km-wide “paleochannel” — a well-preserved mud and sand archive of the river’s ancient course — about 45 km to the south of the modern Ganga river. Today, the area is used to cultivate rice.
Based on geological measures in this area, they found the Ganga had abruptly changed its course — or avulsed — about 2,500 years ago, leaving behind the palaeochannel.
During their fieldwork, the team also chanced upon two large sand dikes a kilometre to the east of the palaeochannel. These dikes are formed when earthquakes disturb the river bed and cause sediments to flow as if they were liquid. Scientists call this process liquefaction.

Modi to become India's longest-serving elected Prime Minister on 10 June, surpassing Nehru
Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to become India's longest-serving elected prime minister on 10 June. With this milestone, PM Modi will overtake Jawaharlal Nehru's tenure as the country's longest-serving elected leader.
PM Modi took oath as prime minister for the first time on 26 May, 2014. He is in his third term as PM and will complete 4,399 consecutive days in office on 10 June.
The record for the longest stint before PM Modi is held by the first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, who served as Prime Minister of India for 16 years and 4,398 days.
Indira Gandhi served as the prime minister of India again from 1980 until her assassination in 1984. She was India's first and, to date, only female prime minister, and a central figure in Indian politics as the leader of the Indian National Congress(INC).
Indira Gandhi was the daughter of Jawaharlal Nehru, the first prime minister of India, and the mother of Rajiv Gandhi, who succeeded her as prime minister. Gandhi's cumulative tenure as prime minister was 15 years and 350 days.

passages.passage:
Diljit Dosanjh Visits Eiffel Tower In Paris, All You Need To Know About The Iconic Landmark
Diljit has now landed in the French capital and given fans a glimpse of his time in the city. Taking to social media, the Punjabi superstar shared a video featuring one of Paris' most recognisable landmarks – the Eiffel Tower.
The Eiffel Tower is among the most famous landmarks in the world and has become synonymous with Paris. Standing at 330 metres (1,083 feet), the tower was originally planned as a 300-metre structure for the 1889 Exposition Universelle, a world fair organised to mark the 100th anniversary of the French Revolution.
All the elements were prepared in Eiffel's factory located at Levallois-Perret on the outskirts of Paris. The structure was assembled using prefabricated metal components. According to the official Eiffel Tower website, around 18,000 individual metal parts were specifically designed and calculated, traced out to an accuracy of a tenth of a millimetre and then put together, forming new pieces around five metres each.

Mumbai: A quiet debate among Maharashtra’s women has now reached the state assembly. First-time NCP MLA Sana Malik Shaikh has called for greater flexibility in how women’s names appear in official records, advocating for the right to retain their maiden and married surnames or to use their mother’s name alongside their father’s.
Speaking in the assembly on Wednesday, the Anushaktinagar MLA—daughter of former minister Nawab Malik—emphasised that women should have the freedom to decide how their names are recorded. Currently, a state government order mandates the inclusion of a mother’s name in official and academic documents. However, Shaikh pointed out that this has led to discomfort among many women, especially those who prefer to retain their married names.

passages.title: Bitcoin's Trump-era rally unravels as cryptocurrency hits two-year low
passages.passage:
Bitcoin's Trump-era rally unravels as cryptocurrency hits two-year low
Bitcoin's rebound was short-lived after the midterm results in early November. Bitcoin was trading near $77,500 before voters went to the polls on November 3. Immediately following the November 3, 2026, US midterm elections, Bitcoin briefly rallied to a peak near $81,196. It fell to an intraday low of about $75,630 on November 4, after Democrats won control of Congress, amid concern that the result could slow new crypto legislation. It quickly recovered, climbing above $80,000 and briefly topping $81,000. The gains did not last. A hotter-than-expected October inflation and looming interest rate hike reading pushed Bitcoin below $74,000, and it had slipped under $73,000 by November 11,The pullback arrives as analysts debate whether the post-election period will follow history. Bitcoin rose 24.5% in the 12 months after the 2014 midterms, 44.9% after 2018 and 92.3% after 2022. Past bottoms came 13 to 71 days after those elections. Some analysts caution that this cycle differs: Bitcoin hit a low near $57,700 in July, months before the vote.

passages.title: Bitcoin’s white paper: A guide
passages.passage:
The origins of cryptocurrency lie in a 14-year-old document written by a person whose identity has not been established. A white paper titled “Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System” describes how an alternative electronic cash system can allow payments to be sent directly from one party to another, without involving trusted parties like a financial institution.
This article, which is now referred to as the Bitcoin Whitepaper, was first released in October 2008 by Satoshi Nakamoto and included important information about how Bitcoin (BTC) may enable a trust-less electronic payment system by utilising cryptographic evidence.
As a result, the first transaction in a block initiates the creation of a new Bitcoin that is held by the block’s author, and nodes continue to assist the network to create more BTCs.
Thus, the Bitcoin White Paper proposed a peer-to-peer transaction network that introduced a revolutionary new way of transacting that was also secure, borderless, and available to all.

passages.title: From CJI To Cabinet Minister: How India's Election Commissioner Selection Process Changed
passages.passage:
From CJI To Cabinet Minister: How India's Election Commissioner Selection Process Changed
The process of appointing India’s Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) has undergone a significant change in the past few years, with the Chief Justice of India (CJI) moving from the selection panel to a Union Cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
That committee was to comprise the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and the Chief Justice of India. If there was no recognised Leader of the Opposition, the leader of the largest opposition party in the Lok Sabha was to be part of the panel instead.
The law retained a three-member selection committee but made one crucial change, that the Chief Justice of India was replaced by a Union Cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
The Supreme Court's March 2023 judgment held that appointments should be made on the advice of a three-member committee including the Chief Justice of India until Parliament enacted a law. Parliament subsequently passed the 2023 Act, which replaced the CJI with a Union Cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister.

passages.title: From CJI To Cabinet Minister: How India's Election Commissioner Selection Process Changed
passages.passage:
From CJI To Cabinet Minister: How India's Election Commissioner Selection Process Changed
The process of appointing India’s Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) has undergone a significant change in the past few years, with the Chief Justice of India (CJI) moving from the selection panel to a Union Cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
That committee was to comprise the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and the Chief Justice of India. If there was no recognised Leader of the Opposition, the leader of the largest opposition party in the Lok Sabha was to be part of the panel instead.
The law retained a three-member selection committee but made one crucial change, that the Chief Justice of India was replaced by a Union Cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
The Supreme Court's March 2023 judgment held that appointments should be made on the advice of a three-member committee including the Chief Justice of India until Parliament enacted a law. Parliament subsequently passed the 2023 Act, which replaced the CJI with a Union Cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister.

The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has rejected speculation about privatising the space agency. Chairman V Narayanan reiterated that “people must not misinterpret that ISRO will be privatised”. He stated that a large chunk of the space agency’s budget goes to the private sector to meet surging global and domestic demand for thousands of satellites.
“The space ecosystem in the country and the country’s economy will grow, resulting in job opportunities. When a Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) or Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV) rocket takes off, 75% of our budget is pumped into the private industries. The private companies are also contributing. People must not misinterpret that as ISRO will be privatised,” Narayanan was quoted as saying by The Hindu.

passages.title: From CJI To Cabinet Minister: How India's Election Commissioner Selection Process Changed
passages.passage:
From CJI To Cabinet Minister: How India's Election Commissioner Selection Process Changed
The process of appointing India’s Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) has undergone a significant change in the past few years, with the Chief Justice of India (CJI) moving from the selection panel to a Union Cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
That committee was to comprise the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and the Chief Justice of India. If there was no recognised Leader of the Opposition, the leader of the largest opposition party in the Lok Sabha was to be part of the panel instead.
The law retained a three-member selection committee but made one crucial change, that the Chief Justice of India was replaced by a Union Cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister.
The Supreme Court's March 2023 judgment held that appointments should be made on the advice of a three-member committee including the Chief Justice of India until Parliament enacted a law. Parliament subsequently passed the 2023 Act, which replaced the CJI with a Union Cabinet minister nominated by the Prime Minister.

The doomsday and nationwide blackout rumors started circulating after US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth revealed the Pentagon's long-term readiness initiative on September 30, per Fox News. The preparation that would allow US military bases to keep operating for at least 90 days without any outside support is a requirement that's part of the FORTRESS America plan.

The FORTRESS America plan is not an announcement of an active nationwide blackout in the US or a power cut that could last for up to 90 days and affect American citizens. Rather, it's the country's prepared plan to ensure that the US's military power "cannot be starved out, shut down, or cut off."

The requirement is part of FORTRESS, a broader military initiative designed to ensure American forces can continue operating even if the civilian infrastructure they depend on is disrupted, according to documents reviewed by Fox News Digital.
Under FORTRESS, every major military installation in the continental United States would be expected to sustain essential operations independently for at least 90 days. This would include maintaining access to electricity, water, fuel and communications even if civilian infrastructure becomes unavailable.
A key focus of FORTRESS is reducing the military's dependence on civilian electricity grids, which support communications, logistics, weapons manufacturing and other essential defence operations.
The initiative also establishes a requirement for at least two qualified supply or production pathways for the military's most critical defence dependencies. The measure is intended to reduce the risk that the loss of a single factory, supplier or industrial capability could interrupt military operations.

In light of renewed debates and discussions about Balochistan within the politics of South Asia, there is a certain date that comes to prominence on a regular basis: August 11. Each year, numerous Baloch national movements celebrate this day as the Independence Day of Balochistan, because it denotes the brief period of time when the Khanate of Kalat existed as an independent state prior to joining Pakistan.
Recently, Baloch representative and diplomat Mir Yar Baloch took to X (formerly Twitter) and shared, "The Republic of Balochistan announces worldwide celebrations of August 11 as the Independence Day of Balochistan with national unity."
While the Baloch nationalists observe August 11 as marking the day of independence for their land, Pakistan claims the legitimacy of its accession in 1948.

passages.title: Power, land, faster clearances: How Indian states are battling for data center investments
passages.passage:
Power, land, faster clearances: How Indian states are battling for data center investments
As India prepares for a sharp expansion in data center capacity, states are competing to offer companies a more attractive place to build. Cheaper power, support for land and construction costs and quicker approvals are central to that contest. A new policy ranking by S&P Global puts Telangana, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh at the front of the race.
Telangana emerges as the key state for data centre investment in S&P Global’s DCPAI index due to a combination of competitive power tariffs, strong regulatory incentives and clear policy frameworks. These measures help lower both upfront capital costs and ongoing operating expenses for data centre developers, giving the state an edge in attracting hyperscalers and large cloud providers.
Maharashtra offers a balanced, broad-based policy package that covers power, infrastructure, capital support and regulatory ease. Its incentives span the entire project lifecycle, making it a stable and predictable destination for data centre investments, particularly for operators looking for a mix of market access, connectivity and policy support.

passages.title: At Ujani Dam, villagers draw a line against AI data centre and solar projects
passages.passage:
At Ujani Dam, villagers draw a line against AI data centre and solar projects
“Whoever is against the construction of the AI data centre, please raise your hands,” came an announcement around 11:30 am on November 13 during a Gram Sabha held in Ranzani village in Maharashtra’s Solapur district, by the banks of the Bhima river. Every villager present, young and old, including onlooking children, raised their hands in unison. “The AI data centre and all remaining projects should be cancelled,” said many.
The projects are a scaled-down version of initial plans that included a green hydrogen plant and a small modular reactor (SMR) nuclear project. After public backlash and citing feasibility concerns, District Collector S. Karthikeyan announced the cancellation of two of the five projects on November 4. The projects are public-private partnerships (PPP) between the State government’s Water Resources Department, JW Global, and The SEED Consortium Partners, with an initial projected investment of Rs.1.65 lakh crore. The 1.4 GW hyperscale data centre represents almost 70 per cent of this investment.

passages.title: Google's Rs 1.35 Lakh Crore Data Centre Project In Andhra Pradesh To Begin April 28
passages.passage:
Google's Rs 1.35 Lakh Crore Data Centre Project In Andhra Pradesh To Begin April 28
Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu will lay the foundation stone for Google's massive data centre project near Visakhapatnam on April 28, marking what is expected to be the biggest foreign investment ever made in India and in Andhra Pradesh.
The project, with an estimated investment of $15 billion (around Rs 1.35 lakh crore), will come up across 601 acres at three locations Adavivaram, Tarluvada and Rambilli near the coastal city of Visakhapatnam. The facility is expected to be fully operational by July 2028.
The proposed hub will have a total power capacity of 1 gigawatt, making it India's first 1-GW artificial intelligence and data centre hub and the largest such cluster in Asia. Officials say the project will support cloud services, artificial intelligence, digital storage and advanced computing. It will also include submarine cable connectivity and high-speed fibre networks linking Visakhapatnam to global digital infrastructure.

As we have noted on multiple occasions, including during the Sixth Committee’s consideration of a new request for observer status several weeks ago, the United States believes it is time for the United Nations to get back to basics, to renew its founding mission to maintain international peace and security, and to rebuild trust across the world that the UN can be a responsible steward of the precious resources that Member States entrust to it. In that context, we believe that “getting back to basics” includes taking a more disciplined approach to considering organizations’ requests for observer status in the General Assembly.
Turning to the specific request[s] up for consideration today, we note that General Assembly Decision 49/426 limits the types of organizations that can be granted observer status in the General Assembly to “intergovernmental organizations whose activities cover matters of interest to the Assembly.”

passages.title: Statement at the 81st General Assembly Sixth Committee Agenda Item 177: Observer status for the Climate Vulnerable Forum
passages.passage:
An official website of the United States government
Official websites use .gov A .gov website belongs to an official government organization in the United States.
As previously noted, General Assembly Decision 49/426 limits the types of organizations that can be granted observer status in the General Assembly to “intergovernmental organizations whose activities cover matters of interest to the Assembly.” Unfortunately, the United States is unable at this time to support the request to grant observer status to the Climate Vulnerable Forum, or CVF. We have outstanding questions regarding whether the CVF is an intergovernmental organization under international law as required by Decision 49/426. We note that the sponsorship letter submitted in support of the CVF states that the Forum has “juridical personality” in light of a headquarters agreement between the Forum itself and the Government of the Republic of Ghana. However, we see no claim made that the CVF has international legal personality — a core attribute of intergovernmental organizations.

passages.title: Chetwode , Dinkar to a Field Marshal baton : How the Army chief office has changed
passages.passage:
Chetwode, Dinkar to a Field Marshal’s baton: How the Army chief’s office has changed
The longest-standing fixture in the Army chief’s office was Field Marshal Philip W Chetwode’s motto, delivered by him at the inauguration of the Indian Military Academy in Dehradun in 1932.
Chetwode’s words remained on the wall for decades, including during General VP Malik’s tenure as Army chief from 1997 to 2000, Malik confirmed to HT.
Dinkar’s verses made way for the Field Marshal’s baton under the current Army chief, General Dhiraj Seth. Portraits of the two military legends have also been replaced with newer versions, recasting the corner as a tribute to India’s Field Marshals.
Seth has made another change. In the adjacent Army chief’s lounge, the painting titled Karam Kshetra—Field of Deeds has been replaced by the Indian Army emblem. The Karam Kshetra artwork had replaced an iconic painting depicting the signing of the Instrument of Surrender at the end of the 1971 war with Pakistan, which led to the liberation of Bangladesh.

passages.title: Could Donald Trump face another impeachment ? Democrats prepare broad probes into White House
passages.passage:
Could Donald Trump face another impeachment? Democrats prepare broad probes into White House
House Democrats are preparing an expansive oversight agenda targeting President Donald Trump and his administration. The proposed investigations would span multiple House committees and could include subpoenas, hearings and, potentially, impeachment proceedings if the party wins control of the House of Representatives in the November midterm elections.
Also read: ‘They have no money coming in, dying’: Donald Trump claims Iran ready to reopen Strait of Hormuz
Democrats plan to scrutinize Trump’s business dealings, the financial interests of his family and the administration’s immigration policies. They also intend to investigate alleged civil rights violations linked to ICE enforcement actions and deportation practices.
Donald Trump made history as the first US president to be impeached twice during a single term in office. The Senate acquitted him on both occasions. Any future impeachment would first need approval by a simple majority in the House before proceeding to a Senate trial, where a two-thirds vote would be required to secure a conviction.

passages.title: US Midterms: If Democrats Win The House And Senate, Can They Remove Trump From Office?
passages.passage:
US Midterms: If Democrats Win The House And Senate, Can They Remove Trump From Office?
If Democrats win both the House and Senate, it would reopen the door to impeaching Donald Trump, though actually removing him from office would remain virtually impossible without significant Republican support. A Democratic victory would also derail Trump's agenda by ending his unchecked control, blocking his legislative plans, and allowing Democrats to launch investigations, hold hearings, and issue subpoenas to probe corruption and federal overreach.
If Democrats win a majority in the House of Representatives in the November midterms, they could approve articles of impeachment against Donald Trump after the new Congress takes office in January 2027. However, actually removing him from office would be virtually impossible for Democrats alone, even if they also win the Senate. Convicting him requires 67 Senate votes, and because only 33 seats are up for election, they would still need a significant number of Republican senators to join them.

Donald Trump likely to make ‘major’ Russia statement as he backs tougher sanctions on Putin's govt
US President Donald Trump said on Thursday he plans to make a “major statement” on Russia. “I think I’ll have a major statement to make on Russia on Monday,” Trump told NBC News in a telephone interview.
Trump's comments came as the US prepares to send a volley of new American weapons to Ukraine via purchases from NATO allies.
In the interview, Trump reiterated criticism of Russian President Vladimir Putin over its continued attacks on Ukraine, Bloomberg reported.
Trump also said he expects the Senate to pass a tougher Russia sanctions bill sponsored by a close ally, Senator Lindsey Graham of South Carolina.
Meanwhile, Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabko said a new round of talks between Russia and the United States on bilateral problems may take place before the end of the summer.

India Is Building Its Fastest-Ever Bullet Train To Match Japan's E10. Here's The Plan
India is getting closer to having its own high-speed bullet train, as Railways are working on the B35, a train designed to reach speeds of up to 350 kmph. The project is part of India's plan to develop more railway technology at home and reduce its dependence on foreign technology.
India is aiming to develop these homegrown bullet trains by 2030 while also building the infrastructure needed to run them.
According to a Times of India report, India began working on the B35 bullet trains after Japan said in December 2024 that it would gradually stop making existing E5 series trains. The country mentioned that production of its newer E10 trains is expected to start in 2030, and the trains will be ready for service by 2034. Indian officials may look at using the E10 trains once they become available.

passages.passage:
India’s bullet train turns indigenous: Features, cost, other details about made-in-India first high-speed rail project
India's dream bullet train project is finally preparing for launch almost a decade after its foundation stone was laid by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. India's first bullet train, which will run between Ahmedabad and Mumbai, is expected become operational from the later half of this year.
As authorities prepare to launch the first leg of this project between Surat and Bilimora, the full project is expected to be completed in 2030. With train sets arriving from Japan, the project’s ₹1.1 lakh crore funding has come from the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA). The Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project is being developed by National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL) with Japanese technology support.

passages.title: 280 kmph, 8 Coaches, 557 Passengers: What Will India's 1st Bullet Train Offer
passages.passage:
280 kmph, 8 Coaches, 557 Passengers: What Will India's 1st Bullet Train Offer
In a historic infrastructural milestone, India is set to roll out its first-ever high-speed Bullet Train, which is being designed and built indigenously for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail (MAHSR) corridor.
The manufacturing process is currently underway at the BEML (Bharat Earth Movers Limited) facility in Bengaluru. Breaking away from complete reliance on foreign technology transfers, Indian engineers have designed this train specifically to withstand the country's unique climatic and operational conditions.
The bullet train is designed to achieve a maximum test speed of 280 km per hour but will run at an operational speed of 249 km per hour. The total length of the train will be 202 metres, with eight coaches including four motor cars and four trailer cars. The train will be able to carry 557 passengers, including two seats designated for Divyangjan or Persons with Reduced Mobility.

passages.title: Firefly Aerospace Is Awarded New Orbital Contract From Department of Defense
passages.passage:
By Eric Volkman – Aug 15, 2026 at 9:50PM EST
Firefly Aerospace (FLY +8.20%) just scored another in a lengthening series of U.S. federal government contracts. Just after market close on Thursday, the space company announced it had signed a pact with the Department of Defense (DoD; rebranded the Department of War by the Trump administration) for the first phase of a planned mission.
The contract, issued by the Department's Defense Innovation Unit and its Space Development Agency, covers a preliminary design review (PDR) for a deorbit mission (for those unfamiliar, deorbiting is the process of clearing space debris from operational orbits).
And that's likely the main reason for the tepid investor reaction on Friday. This, plus the fact that Firefly is actively working on dozens of contracts, some of which are in far more advanced stages than this new one. In fact, the space company took pains to note that it's currently under contract with the Defense Innovation Unit for a space domain awareness mission. This will be undertaken with the Elytra, the same spacecraft that will be used if and when the company advances to later stages of the deorbit project.

passages.passage:
New Delhi: A 55-year-old man was killed after a speeding Mahindra Thar, allegedly driven by a woman learner driver, rammed his electric scooter in Uttar Pradesh's Kanpur on Saturday evening, November 7, on the eve of Diwali. The victim, identified as Santosh Kumar Singh Chauhan, was returning home with a saree for his wife when the accident took place barely 500 metres from his residence.
According to his son, Rahul Chauhan, Santosh had left home on his scooter to purchase a saree for his wife. He had told his family that he would return shortly. However, the family received news of his death soon after the accident.
According to eyewitness accounts, the Mahindra Thar was travelling at high speed when it rammed into Santosh's scooter. The impact reportedly dragged the two-wheeler for approximately 25 to 30 metres before the SUV crashed into a railing and boundary walls.
The identity of the woman allegedly driving the Thar and the circumstances surrounding the accident remain under investigation. Further investigation is underway.

A 24-year-old woman who ran over and killed a 55-year-old LIC agent with her Mahindra Thar in Kanpur over the weekend was granted bail on Diwali, prompting the victim's son to question the justice system.
The accident took place on November 7, on the eve of Diwali, when Santosh Singh Chauhan was returning home on his scooter after purchasing a saree for his wife. The impact of the speeding Thar, driven by Geeta Sachan, was so severe that Santosh died on the spot. The SUV hit the scooter and dragged both Santosh and his vehicle for a few metres, police said.
"What kind of justice is this? The woman who killed my father and brought darkness into our home just before Diwali is celebrating the festival with her family after being released. What about the darkness in our house?" Rahul Chauhan, the victim's son, said.

Nepal flash floods: Did earthquakes trigger the avalanche that left at least 22 dead and hundreds missing?
Several visuals from Nepal have emerged online, as an avalanche of ice and rock triggered massive flash floods in the Himalayan country on Wednesday. Rasuwa district, bordering Tibet, remains the worst affected, with villages and infrastructure swept away. Primary reports claim that an earthquake might have caused the avalanche on the Lhende Khola river, which runs through both Nepal and Tibet, leading to severe flooding in the region, according to a Reuters report.
Nepal’s Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal told Parliament that initial reports suggested an earthquake in the affected region may have triggered an avalanche, which in turn led to the floods, as per local media.

passages.passage:
People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals euthanized approximately 67% of the animals that it took in during the year 2024.
Social media users claimed that PETA euthanized 2,213 out of the 3,317 animals it took in that year.
The Virginia Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services' database of animal custody record reports for PETA in the year 2024 shows a total of 3,317 companion animals taken in, including 1,374 dogs and 1,885 cats. Of the total number, the data shows 2,709 of the animals were classified as "surrendered by owner."
Of those 3,317 animals, 2,213 were euthanized, making the percentage of animals euthanized by PETA that year 66.7% (which rounds up to 67%).
PETA's services also span 260 localities across Virginia and North Carolina. So naturally, our intake—and by extension our euthanasia figures—will be higher than shelters that serve only their specific locality, because we are assisting exponentially more animals, including those from communities far beyond Norfolk's borders.

Electric vehicle major Tesla is reportedly developing an all-new, compact electric SUV that would be smaller and significantly cheaper than its current entry-level models, according to a Reuters report. The project is said to mark a renewed push into the affordable EV segment, coming two years after CEO Elon Musk had shelved an earlier low-cost EV programme widely associated with the so called "Model 2" concept.

Argentina’s poverty rate rose to 32.3% in the first half of 2026 from 28.2% in the previous six months, official data showed on Thursday, as incomes lagged rising prices. Extreme poverty climbed to 7.5% from 6.3%. Among children aged 14 and under, 44.5% were poor.
Argentina's poverty rate increased to 32.3 percent in the first half of 2026, partly erasing gains made under President Javier Milei as incomes fail to keep step with rising prices, official statistics showed Thursday.
The rate grew 4.1 points compared to the last half of 2025, the national statistics agency Indec said.
The rate of extreme poverty also shot up from 6.3 percent to 7.5 percent.
The figures deal a setback to Milei, a free-market radical, who nearly halved the poverty rate during the first two years of his mandate, mainly by shrinking perennially high inflation.

'Final call': Dipke releases video message ahead of CJP protest, anticipates arrest upon landing in Delhi
CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, in a final video appeal ahead of the protest at Jantar Mantar over CEC row in Delhi on October 10, said he was unsure whether he would be arrested upon landing in the national capital but asserted that he would not back down from the fight for free and fair elections.
The CJP is leading a massive demonstration at Jantar Mantar on Saturday to demand the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
"I am not scared (even) if I am detained or arrested. The government can slap NSA or UAPA against me. CJP wants free and fair polls and that cannot happen without (Chief Election Commissioner) Gyanesh Kumar's resignation or scrapping of SIR or neutral procedure to appoint election commissioner," he said, asking people to come to Jantar Mantar in large numbers.
“This is a fight to save our country's democracy,” Dipke said, reiterating the CJP's demand for free and fair elections.

passages.title: CJP to 'restrategise after Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka's release': Abhijeet Dipke on anti-CEC stir
passages.passage:
CJP to 'restrategise after Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka's release': Abhijeet Dipke on anti-CEC stir
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke stated on Sunday that the outfit will 'gather, restrategise, and determine its next steps' amid protests in Delhi against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Election Commission of India's (ECI) Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.
Dipke noted that once CJP members Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were previously remanded to judicial custody, return, they will formally decide how to move forward, according to news agency ANI.
The CJP founder said, "Once Saurav and Ashu come, we will gather, restrategise, and determine how to move forward. Given what we have witnessed over the past few days, including the illegal arrests and detentions, it is clear that there is an attempt to intimidate us."
"However, we will neither be intimidated nor back down. This is a long battle, and we are fully prepared for it. Hopefully, both of them will be released today," Dipke said.

passages.title: ‘Jantar Mantar at Kochi’: CJP announces anti-SIR stir on November 7; Dipke to attend
passages.passage:
‘Jantar Mantar at Kochi’: CJP announces anti-SIR stir on November 7; Dipke to attend
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Thursday announced an anti-Special Intensive Revision (SIR) protest in Kochi, Kerala, on November 7, renewing the call for the cancellation of the voter roll revision exercise. The protest, titled “Jantar Mantar at Kochi”, will be held at Rajendra Maidan from 4 pm, CJP said in a post on X.
“Save Democracy! Cancel SIR! Join Us - 7th November - 4 PM | Rajendra Maidan, Kochi,” the post read.
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke will be part of the demonstration. Vijay Mallangi, the group's south zone lead, and Aafreen Nawaz, its national secretary, will also attend the anti-SIR protest in Kochi on November 7.
The protest in Kochi marks CJP's first major move since its leaders were arrested in Delhi while attempting to stage a demonstration at Jantar Mantar against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and SIR of electoral rolls.
CJP extended its support to the INDIA bloc's march in Delhi on November 1 but did not participate in the Rahul Gandhi-led rally at Ramlila Maidan.

passages.title: CJP to launch nationwide protest from Oct 2, seeks Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation
passages.passage:
CJP to launch nationwide protest from Oct 2, seeks Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation
Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke has announced a nationwide agitation from October 2 over alleged irregularities in electoral rolls, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and greater accountability in the functioning of the Election Commission.
Dipke on Thursday said the agitation will begin with a protest in Mumbai on Gandhi Jayanti and will subsequently be taken to different parts of the country before culminating in a sit-in at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. The CJP’s demands include freezing the 2025 electoral roll, holding elections on its basis and introducing a transparent process for appointing the next Election Commissioner.
“The CJP’s three principal demands are the resignation of Kumar, freezing of the electoral roll prepared in 2025 and holding elections on the basis of that roll, and a transparent and independent process for appointing the next Election Commissioner, with participation from civil society,” he said.

The widow of Charlie Kirk, the conservative activist assassinated on a college campus last week, was unanimously elected on Thursday as the new CEO of Turning Point USA, the group Kirk founded to galvanize young voters to Republican causes.

passages.title: Flanagan heads to U.S. Senate, shaped by generations of Native women leaders
passages.passage:
Create an account or log in to save stories.
More than two decades ago, at an education event at the Minneapolis American Indian Center, Peggy Flanagan took the microphone and offered to help anyone who wanted to run for the Minneapolis school board. Franny Fairbanks, the center’s longtime director, had a question for her.
On Tuesday, Flanagan won Minnesota’s open U.S. Senate seat, defeating Republican Michele Tafoya. The seat opened when Sen. Tina Smith decided not to seek reelection.
But Flanagan is far from the first Native woman in Minnesota to lead. For generations, Native women have led their nations and their communities, pushing for better schools, early childhood education, housing, public safety and treaty rights. They have also passed that leadership on, the way Fairbanks tapped Flanagan to run for school board.
“I could not run for the U.S. Senate without Native women. I could not exist in the way that I do without Native women,” Flanagan said.

passages.passage: Chronic pain is a complex health condition wherein persistent pain is experienced for months, even years, without a definite cause. According to the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and affiliated bodies like the National Centre for Disease Informatics and Research (NCDIR), chronic pain is emerging as a major public health issue in India due to the startling figures. The figures indicate a steep rise, as about 19 to 25% of Indian adults report chronic pain lasting more than 3 months. Out of this figure, women are disproportionately affected, with the recorded rates nearly 1.5 times higher than men, especially pain in the bones, muscles, joints, tendons, and ligaments, and due to nervous system dysfunction.

passages.title: Covid-19 lockdowns caused more chronic pain in women than men. Here's why
passages.passage:
Covid-19 lockdowns caused more chronic pain in women than men. Here's why
A new study has found that the pandemic lockdown caused an increase in chronic pain, especially in women.
"With chronic pain affecting around 20 per cent of the EU adult population, it is vital to understand how people living with chronic pain are being affected by the pandemic and to develop pain management interventions that clearly target women," Lang-Illievich added.
Responses indicated that women with chronic pain perceived increased pain severity during the first lockdown, compared to their typical pain levels prior to lockdown. While average pain intensity scored (VAS 0-100) before the first COVID-19 lockdown was similar in men (46.5) and women (45), the average change in pain intensity was much lower in men (0.8) than women (3.9).
"Although reported pain intensity between men and women was similar before COVID-19, our data clearly show that women experienced a higher aggravation of chronic pain during the first lockdown," said Lang-Illievich.

Russian President Vladimir Putin has long insisted on a rethink of European defense, demanding that NATO pull back its forces and that Russia be given a key voice in the continent's security — calls that predate the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.
“Security guarantees for Ukraine cannot be finalized in isolation from post-war European security architecture. The two must be considered together,” Trump's peace envoy Jared Kushner wrote Sunday.
The Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe, headquartered in Vienna, is one of the few European security bodies Russia still belongs to.
“We need to make full use of this unique platform to preserve dialogue, rebuild transparency, reduce risks and manage tensions,” OSCE Secretary-General Feridun Sinirlioğlu told POLITICO. “The OSCE remains a key forum for rebuilding a more stable and predictable security architecture in Europe.”

passages.title: How data centres became one of America’s hottest political issues
passages.passage:
How data centres became one of America’s hottest political issues
A little over a year ago some polls showed majority support for local data-centre construction. By March that had flipped: one Gallup poll found 71% opposed. Surveys by Annenberg recorded a 19-point swing in net favourability between February and June-July. An Economist/YouGov poll from the end of August put opposition at 63%. Data centres were viewed as bad for the country across every group of voters (see chart 1).
The growing opposition is sand in the wheels of the industry. Sales-tax exemptions for computer chips—the biggest cost of building a new data centre—remain in place in most states, including Texas. But they have been paused in others, including Arizona and Ohio, or made conditional, as in Pennsylvania. That, along with satisfying local demands, will inevitably increase the cost of new data centres. Even so, a handful of states still wield outsize influence. Texas alone has more data centres under construction than Georgia, Arizona and Pennsylvania combined (see chart 3).

Election officials in Mississippi were racing Friday to verify thousands of outstanding ballots in a razor-thin US Senate race, three days after Democrats swept to power in a historic defeat for President Donald Trump's Republicans.
The unusually prolonged count reflects Mississippi's election procedures, which allow officials several days to process mail-in and provisional ballots -- potentially enough to decide the contest.
These are cast by people whose eligibility cannot be confirmed at polling stations, sometimes because of missing identification or discrepancies in voter registration records.
Voters have until Tuesday to resolve certain problems with their ballots. Mail votes postmarked by Election Day can also arrive through Tuesday, while Mississippi's 82 counties have until November 13 to certify their results.
Mississippi has not elected a Democratic senator since 1982, and Colom would be its first Black senator since the Reconstruction era following the American Civil War.
The stakes have diminished nationally, however, after Democrats captured both chambers of Congress in Tuesday's midterm elections, securing their Senate majority without needing Mississippi.

Supreme Court President Isaac Amit and Justices Alex Stein and Khaled Kabub noted that about one year and nine months had passed since the start of Operation Iron Wall, the IDF operation launched in the northern West Bank back in January 2025. Can the Chief Election Commissioner be removed? What the law says
Opposition parties are demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities and biased conduct
The Constitution dictates that the Chief Election Commissioner can only be removed through the same procedure and grounds as a Supreme Court judge
The recent wave of protests by the Opposition parties, political outfits and the Cockroach Janta Party, are demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities and biased conduct. The Opposition is even considering an impeachment motion against the CEC. The question of what happens when the guardian of the ballot box becomes the subject of a removal demand arises. In India, public outrage may raise the question and demand accountability, but the Constitution has the answer.

passages.passage:
Andhra Pradesh villages give a reality check to India’s 2030 malaria elimination target
All cells in the body, including tumour cells, shed DNA into the bloodstream when they die. Multi-cancer early detection tests look for the trace amounts of tumour DNA in the bloodstream. This circulating “cell-free” DNA contains information about what type of tissue it came from and whether it is normal or cancerous.
Multi-cancer early detection tests are different from existing liquid biopsies because they are trying to detect early-stage cancer, when there aren’t that many tumour cells yet. Detecting these cancer cells can be challenging early on because non-cancer cells also shed DNA into the bloodstream. Since most of the circulating DNA in the bloodstream comes from non-cancer cells, detecting the presence of a few molecules of cancer DNA is like finding a needle in a haystack.
Making things even more difficult, blood cells shed abnormal DNA naturally with ageing, and these strands can be confused for circulating cancer DNA. This phenomenon, known as clonal hematopoiesis, confounded early attempts at developing multi-cancer early detection tests, with too many false positive results.

Hours before polls opened for the US midterm elections, the FBI's New Haven field office told voters the wrong date for Election Day in a post promoting the bureau's work to protect the vote.
'Election day is Wednesday and the #FBI is working around the clock to ensure the midterms are safe,' the account wrote on X at about 4:00 p.m. ET on Monday, 2 November, roughly 14 hours before Connecticut's polling places opened.
Election Day is Tuesday, 3 November. Federal law fixes the general election on the Tuesday after the first Monday in November, and Connecticut polls are open from 6:00 a.m. to 8:00 p.m., according to the office of Governor Ned Lamont.
By late Monday, X users had attached a Community Note stating that Election Day falls on Tuesday, 3 November. Its second line read: 'Not Wednesday'.

The post, published on the official FBI New Haven X account on Nov. 2, said: “Election day is Wednesday and the #FBI is working around the clock to ensure the midterms are safe.” Federal Election Day in 2026 was Tuesday, Nov. 3. The FBI later said the post contained a typo and had been removed once the error was identified.
The concrete record ends with the state’s correction and the bureau’s removal of the message: the official FBI New Haven account published the wrong Election Day, Connecticut said so publicly, and the correct date was Tuesday, Nov. 3, 2026.

Syrian President's Father's Statue In A Main Square Toppled By Protesters
Protesters brought down the statue of the late father of Syrian President Bashar al-Assad in a main square in Jermana suburb, nearly ten kilometers from the centre of Damascus, a witness and activists told Reuters.
The protesters in the mainly Druze inhabited suburb, who called for the downfall of Assad, also headed to government buildings in the heavily policed area of the capital where several security branches are located, they said.
The protesters headed to security offices to demand they evacuate from their area, activist Ryan Marouf, editor of Suwayda 24, a website that covers the province, told Reuters.
The authorities have tolerated most protests by the country's Druze minority, unlike in other government-held areas where demonstrators are fired on by security forces.
In a rare act of defiance in areas under Assad's rule, protesters also tore down posters of Assad, where the party has promoted a personality cult around him and his late father, former president Hafez al-Assad.

Katie Zacharia out as White House press secretary after just 5 days on the job: Reports
Katie Zacharia, political commentator turned White House Press Secretary, has been let go of her role in the Donald Trump administration on Friday, the New York Times reported.
The NYT cited five people familiar with the matter to report that Zacharia has been let go from her White House role effective immediately. The report came moments after Trump said before boarding Air Force One Friday that he had asked Zacharia to “reconsider” if she wants to continue as the White House Press Secretary.
Zacharia became the White House Press Secretary on October 10. In her six days in office, she has faced intense media scrutiny over her bar credentials.
Zacharia's departure makes her the shortest-serving White House Press Secretary after Anthony Scaramucci, who served only 11 days as the White House Director of Communications in the previous Trump administration.
Zacharia's credentials to practise law in the United States were questioned after she described herself as a law-practitioner before entering politics. Trump, announcing her nomination to the role, referred to her as an "attorney".

Former White House press secretary Katie Zacharia said in remarks published on Friday that she was “not fired,” challenging reports about how her five-day tenure in President Donald Trump’s administration ended.
Reuters initially reported that two White House officials said she had been “let go” following scrutiny of her briefings and legal background.
Newsweek emailed the White House for further comment on Saturday morning.
A press secretary speaks for the president and is expected to give accurate information under intense public scrutiny, making clarity about the circumstances of an incumbent’s departure significant.
Before Zacharia, a conservative commentator and former communications adviser for Trump Media & Technology Group, took office, the White House went 45 days without a press secretary following Karoline Leavitt’s August 27 departure.

Jantar Mantar: From astronomical observatory to landmark protest site
The Delhi Jantar Mantar, originally known as Yantra Mantra, was built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II of Jaipur as an astronomical observatory at the behest of Mughal emperor Muhammad Shah. Constructed around 1724, it relied on naked-eye observations, with its instruments, or yantras, providing remarkably accurate readings.
Its location, less than 3 km from Parliament, has made Jantar Mantar a symbolic alternative to marches towards Parliament. The site allows demonstrators to voice their concerns within close proximity of the country’s political establishment while remaining outside Parliament’s high-security perimeter. Its nearness to Parliament has also enabled political leaders and legislators to step out of the House and directly address protesters.
Thousands of people opposing the Citizenship (Amendment) Act and the proposed National Register of Citizens gathered at Jantar Mantar on December 19, 2019, after police prevented rallies from proceeding from locations including Mandi House and the Red Fort.

passages.title: INDIA bloc supporters gather at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan for 'Chalo Dilli' protest
passages.passage:
INDIA bloc supporters gather at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan for 'Chalo Dilli' protest
Supporters of various INDIA bloc parties gathered at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan on Sunday for the Opposition alliance's 'Chalo Dilli' protest against alleged electoral irregularities and to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
The leaders travelled in an open bus to Minto Road, from where the march to Ramlila Maidan was scheduled to begin around noon.
Ahead of the protest, Rahul Gandhi urged people travelling to Delhi to support local businesses by shopping from small traders in the run-up to Diwali, Chhath and Bhai Dooj. In a video message posted on X on Saturday, he said the rally would not hurt businesses and encouraged participants to combine their protest with shopping.
The INDIA bloc has estimated that up to 10 lakh people could attend the mobilisation, while Delhi Police expects around 50,000. Ramlila Maidan can accommodate 45,000 to 50,000 people when empty, but its effective capacity is expected to fall to 30,000-40,000 with chairs, enclosures and designated passageways in place. Additional space outside the ground has been earmarked for crowds.

passages.title: INDIA bloc to hold ‘Chalo Dilli’ march at Ramlila Maidan today
passages.passage:
INDIA bloc to hold ‘Chalo Dilli’ march at Ramlila Maidan today
The INDIA bloc will hold a ‘Chalo Dilli’ march at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on November 1, protesting alleged electoral irregularities and the SIR exercise while demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation. Rahul Gandhi and K.C. Venugopal have mobilised public support
New Delhi: The INDIA bloc is set to organise a large-scale ‘Chalo Dilli’ march culminating at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on Sunday to protest alleged electoral irregularities, oppose the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.
Police and paramilitary personnel are also set to be deployed at Ramlila Maidan, with security arrangements tightened ahead of the opposition gathering. Ahead of the rally, Lok Sabha Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi appealed to people travelling to Delhi to join the march and support local traders during the festive season.
Congress MP and party General Secretary (Organisation) K.C. Venugopal had also appealed to people across the country to join the November 1 rally, targeting the BJP-led Centre over the alleged irregularities in the SIR exercise.

passages.title: Kerala CM To Join INDIA Bloc's 'Chalo Dilli' Protest On Nov 1
passages.passage:
Kerala CM To Join INDIA Bloc's 'Chalo Dilli' Protest On Nov 1
Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan will join the INDIA bloc’s ‘Chalo Dilli’ march to Ramlila Maidan on November 1 to protest against alleged electoral irregularities
Kerala Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan confirmed his participation in the INDIA bloc’s 'Chalo Dilli' mega rally at Ramlila Maidan on November 1.
Kerala Chief Minister V D Satheesan will participate in the INDIA bloc's 'Chalo Dilli' protest in New Delhi on Saturday "to defend democracy and the Constitution" and raise concerns over alleged voter list irregularities.
"This is not just a protest. It is a firm declaration that we will not remain silent when democracy is under threat," he said, calling upon people to join the 'Chalo Dilli' protest on November 1.
Congress leader Rahul Gandhi recently urged people to join the opposition INDIA bloc's November 1 'Chalo Dilli' march, asking them not to worry about police and their "lathis".
